metadata.title: Measure-only preserving Markov transports characterize mass-stationarity
metadata.description:
This research note gives an affirmative answer to Last and Thorisson's formal Problem 7.3 (Annals of Probability, 2009). On any locally compact second countable Hausdorff Abelian group, for an arbitrary jointly measurable ambient flow, a sigma-finite measure Q and a nonzero covariant locally finite Radon random measure xi, full ambient invariance under every invariant xi-preserving xi-measurable Markov transport is equivalent to joint mass-stationarity. The proof derives the joint Mecke identity using oriented local symmetric transports away from measure periods and normalized period-subgroup transports. It requires neither a standard Borel ambient space, a sigma-finite marginal law of xi nor finite intensity. The classical Mecke/Palm and Palm/mass-stationarity equivalences and converse transport invariance are credited. The narrower non-discrete deterministic Cox-allocation converse is not claimed.

Two independent extensive bounded priority reviews and a fresh adjudication identified no exact earlier resolution in the sources inspected. This is not an exhaustive literature certificate, worldwide-firstness guarantee or certification of present openness. Unread final editions, including the final 2015 SPA body, and identified audiovisual and citation-coverage gaps are disclosed in the supporting priority note. Statements cited from author editions are not asserted identical to unread final versions.

The verification archive contains the standalone manuscript source, claim and credit records, priority qualifications, unchanged original author and independent finite exact control programs, complete expected outputs and a portable hash-and-output verifier. The finite controls cover examples of preservation, reversal gates, period kernels and hidden ambient states. Legacy background-Cox controls do not certify the stricter intensity-erased Cox-allocation question. Finite computation supplements the analytic proof and proves neither the general theorem nor novelty. AI tools were used extensively in derivation, literature comparison, reproduction, writing and independent adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint without human peer review or a formal proof-assistant certificate.
